name: Kenani
title: Levite who led worship
summary: Kenani was a Levite who served in Jerusalem after the return from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in connection with the public penitence and worship service led by the Levites, where the people confessed their sins and worshipped the Lord. His name means 'my helper' or is linked to Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Participation in the public penitence service
keyEvents.description: Kenani was among the Levites who cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God during the great penitence service that the people held after hearing the words of the law.

keyEvents.title: Call to worship
keyEvents.description: Kenani and the other Levites encouraged the people to stand up and praise the Lord their God from everlasting to everlasting, leading the great prayer of praise.

keyEvents.title: The Levites' prayer of confession
keyEvents.description: As part of the group of Levites, Kenani took part in the long prayer that reviewed Israel's history, God's faithfulness, and the people's disobedience.

keyEvents.title: Renewal of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: After the day of confession, Kenaniah and the Levites led the people in renewing their covenant with God and committing themselves to keep His commands.

keyEvents.title: The Service of the Levites in Rebuilt Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Kenaniah was part of the Levitical service restored during the reforms of Nehemiah and Ezra, when worship in the temple was reorganized.
